name: Reverse Conversion
summary: Short 100 shares, sell a put and buy a call at the same strike - the mirror of a conversion, used to capture put-call parity dislocations on the other side.

legs.strike_rule: same strike as the put, same expiry

max_profit: fixed at entry: share proceeds + put credit - call cost - strike x 100, adjusted for borrow and dividends
max_loss: the same constant if negative; plus unbounded operational risk from a hard-to-borrow buy-in
when_to_use: When the synthetic long is cheap relative to the stock, typically in hard-to-borrow names where the borrow rate IS the dislocation. FLAGGED: not usable at level 3, requires short stock, and the short put is uncovered. Include for completeness only.
entry_rules: BLOCKED: requires (a) a margin account with short-sale capability and an available borrow, and (b) options level 4 for the uncovered short put (the short stock covers it economically but not under standard retail approval).
If ever enabled: require edge >= $0.20 per share net of borrow cost for the full holding period, and require the borrow rate to be locked, not indicative.
management_rules: Monitor the borrow rate daily; a rate spike destroys the trade's economics.
Unwind immediately on any buy-in notice.
Nothing else to manage - the position is delta-flat.
exit_rules: Unwind all three legs as one combo before expiration; never carry into expiry because of pin risk at the shared strike.

Close if the short put's extrinsic < 0.05 (early exercise of the put would deliver 100 long shares, closing the short stock - actually benign, but it ends the arbitrage early and forfeits remaining edge).
Unwind before any ex-dividend date: the short stock position owes the dividend.
assignment_risk: The short put is assignable; assignment delivers 100 long shares which offset the short stock position, ending the trade. The more serious risks are the dividend obligation on the short shares and a forced buy-in on a hard-to-borrow name, which can happen at any time and at any price.
buying_power: Short stock margin (Reg-T 150% of proceeds) plus the option requirement. Level 4.
liquidity_needs: Tight three-leg markets plus a real borrow - rarely available to retail.
common_mistakes: Ignoring borrow cost and dividend obligations; assuming the short stock leg is always maintainable.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
